title: Automatic updates on macOS and Linux
objective: Released Luxforge finds, verifies and installs its newer releases from day one: Sparkle on macOS with a drag-to-Applications disk image and a move into Applications, an in-house payload updater on Linux, one signed feed per target on the backend API under api.luxforge.app/v1/updates/, update.* commands and preferences, and a clean launch past a catalog the new version cannot open.
context_summary: Owner decisions of 2026-10-12, recorded in the design and decisions: no launcher; Sparkle 2 on macOS; in-house Linux updater with notify-only fallback; Windows later on the same feed, key and commands; feeds served by the one backend API under https://api.luxforge.app/v1/updates/; check automatically by default and offer, with automatic installation off by default; the catalog format was reset to 1 and catalog migrations are required from 1.0.0 onwards, so until then a catalog-format-changing update is flagged and never installed automatically. The owner authorized implementation on 2026-10-12, Linux first and then macOS. Routine layout, wording, module and command naming, the update store and publication mechanism, and disk image appearance are delegated within the design. Owner inputs: generating and storing the update key, the production API with its update store and publication credential, release-candidate tags and an authorized foreground clean-install session; they affect only the final qualification task. Implementation never creates, reads or exports production keys, pushes tags or deploys the backend. Use the roadmap's high-tier model minimum and re-review current main before each task.

tasks.description: Define the update feed and per-release update records, and build their signing and feed generation in xtask.
extra_context: Add release/update.json with the feed base URL https://api.luxforge.app/v1/updates/ (the backend API route, beside /v1/usage/batches) and the update public key (absent until the operator commits it); it is the single source for the macOS SUPublicEDKey and the Linux compiled constant.

Per release, write luxforge-<version>-updates.json: per archive target, file name, byte length, build number, Ed25519 signature in Sparkle's edSignature form, minimum OS, catalog format and channel (prerelease for SemVer pre-release tags). Sign only final archives; the private key comes from a file or environment variable named on the command line, never from source or logs.

Generate one Sparkle-format appcast per target (macos-arm64, linux-x86_64) from a directory of published releases' update records, with the luxforge:catalogFormat element in a Luxforge namespace and the GitHub release asset URLs. Refuse build numbers that do not rise with versions, macOS records not marked notarized, and records for unpublished assets; honour a checked-in withdrawal list.
Accept the private-key format the pinned Sparkle generate_keys exports. Command names and module layout are delegated.

tasks.description: Add the core update model: the update port, update.* commands, update preferences and the pre-release channel flag.
extra_context: The core owns state, commands and preferences; a host port in HostConfig performs the platform mechanism. luxforge-json and development builds have no port and report unavailable with a reason.

Methods: update.status (read), update.check (outcome reported without the owner or UI thread waiting on the network), update.install (ClientAuthority::Permissions; not-ready without an update; conflict naming running jobs), update.skip {version}, update.move-to-applications (macOS, Permissions). Register them in METHODS with host_params! schemas.

Preferences update_checks (default true) and update_install_automatically (default false) through preferences.set; a skipped version in the same configuration. Experiments flag updates.prerelease-channel, off by default.

State includes mechanism, reason, current version/build, preferences, last check time/outcome, available update (version, build, notes URL, catalog-format change, skipped), progress, readiness and last error. An update whose catalog format differs from CATALOG_FORMAT is marked and never installed automatically.
Install runs through the ordinary quit path: the port is told to install only after the owner has closed the catalog.

tasks.description: Let the desktop launch past an unsupported remembered catalog and offer a new one.
extra_context: Today a refused remembered catalog fails the launch (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/lifecycle.rs). Instead open the window with a sheet naming the refused catalog's format and the current one, with Start a new catalog and Quit, and a releases-page link through the checked HTTPS opener.

Start a new catalog creates and remembers a new catalog beside the refused one (naming delegated). The refused catalog is never modified, renamed or deleted. An explicit --catalog keeps today's command-line refusal.

tasks.description: Build the Linux payload updater and its desktop port.
extra_context: New crate (name delegated) used only by the desktop: read the feed through luxforge-net, choose the newest followed-channel item with a higher build number, stream to a staging directory beside the payload within the stated length, verify Ed25519 against the compiled public key without heap-holding the archive, extract into Luxforge.new/ refusing absolute paths, '..', escaping links, devices and oversize archives, preserving modes, and check build.json.

Install at the end of the quit path after the catalog closes: renameat2 RENAME_EXCHANGE where supported, else two renames; keep Luxforge.previous until the new version's first successful launch; exec the new executable with the launch arguments (none when installing automatically at quit). Refresh a user-level desktop entry that points at this payload.

Unwritable payload or parent, cross-filesystem staging or a package-manager marker gives linux-notify, whose offer opens the release page. Failures clean staging and leave the payload untouched. Cancel downloads on quit; bounded memory throughout.

tasks.description: Embed Sparkle in the macOS release bundle and bridge it to the update port with a custom user driver.
extra_context: Pin the latest stable Sparkle 2 (2.9 or later): xtask fetches the official archive verified by SHA-256; add its licence to the notices. Embed Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework with Autoupdate and Updater.app, removing the XPC services. Info.plist gains SUFeedURL, SUPublicEDKey, SUEnableAutomaticChecks true, SUScheduledCheckInterval 86400, SUVerifyUpdateBeforeExtraction, and SURequireSignedFeed if the feed can be signed in the workflow (record the outcome in the design).
Sign Autoupdate, Updater.app and the framework before the helpers and app, never recursively.

Load the framework at run time from the bundle; absent framework means unavailable. Implement SPUUserDriver in Rust with objc2, forwarding events into the port state and answering reply blocks from update.* commands; apply Luxforge's preferences to Sparkle every launch and change; filter channels; never install a catalog-format-changing item silently; postpone relaunch until the quit path closed the catalog.
Report outside-applications while the bundle runs from a translocated, disk-image or read-only location.

tasks.description: Offer to move Luxforge into Applications on macOS.
extra_context: For person-launched release builds: detect translocation (SecTranslocateIsTranslocatedURL, as LetsMove does), a disk image or read-only volume, or a location outside /Applications and ~/Applications. Ask with Move and relaunch, Not now, and a Don't ask again preference; never ask in background or evidence launches.

Move: copy preserving the signature into /Applications, or ~/Applications when it is not writable; confirm before trashing an existing Luxforge in the way; clear the copy's quarantine as LetsMove does; relaunch from the new place; trash the original or eject its disk image. update.move-to-applications performs the same operation.

tasks.description: Publish update records and feeds from the release workflow, and document the operator steps.
extra_context: In the publish job, before the draft is published: sign the final archives in a step that alone receives LUXFORGE_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY and upload luxforge-<version>-updates.json with the other assets. Skip macOS records for builds that are not notarized.

After publication succeeds, a feed job regenerates every target's appcast from all published releases' records and publishes them to the backend API's update store, with a scoped credential only that step receives (store and mechanism delegated to the backend deployment). A failed feed publication never alters the release.

The API serves GET /v1/updates/<target>/appcast.xml as static content: no query string, cookies or authentication, cache headers that let a release reach clients within an hour, and no record of client addresses, headers or bodies. Add the route to the backend's deployment checklist and its local reference so it can be exercised before production exists.

Operator guide: generating the update key with the pinned Sparkle generate_keys, committing the public key to release/update.json, storing the private key secret, keeping an offline backup and the consequence of losing it, provisioning the update store and publication credential on the production API, withdrawing a release. Use pinned actions and least permissions.

tasks.description: Qualify updates on real signed candidates and bring the documentation current.
extra_context: Needs owner inputs: the committed update public key and secret, the production api.luxforge.app with its update store and publication credential, two release-candidate tags on the pre-release channel, an owner-authorized foreground session on a clean account or second Mac, and native Ubuntu 24.04. Prepare everything else first and record what remains unrun.

Qualify: M4 update from one candidate to the next with the pre-release flag; DMG install, move into Applications and update on the clean account; native Linux payload update and notify fallback; the feed route answering over HTTPS; a catalog-format-changing offer and the unsupported-catalog launch.
